skill.description: Extract structured Google Images metadata through the BrowserAct API using keyword, region, language, scroll depth, and result limit settings.
skill.summary: Runs a BrowserAct Google Images workflow and returns structured image result metadata.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill performs legitimate BrowserAct API calls for Google Images metadata, and most Markdown backtick detections are false positives. The main security concern is credential handling: the documentation and script output encourage users to provide a BrowserAct API key directly, which can expose secrets in chat logs.

remediation.issue: User-facing instructions request direct API key provision.
remediation.suggestion: Revise SKILL.md and script output to instruct users only to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in their environment or secret manager, and explicitly warn not to paste API keys into chat.

remediation.issue: The skill sends user search terms and bearer authentication to BrowserAct.
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party network dependency and advise users not to submit sensitive or private search terms unless approved by their organization.

remediation.issue: The invocation guidance runs a local Python script.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the command path fixed, quote user-provided arguments when invoking from a shell, and avoid constructing shell commands from raw user input.

content.value_statement: Manual image search is slow when teams need repeatable result metadata across regions. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to collect image titles, thumbnails, source names, and links from Google Images.
actual_capabilities: Runs a Python script that starts a BrowserAct Google Images workflow.
Accepts search keywords, country, language, scroll count, and maximum item count.
Polls BrowserAct task status and reports progress while the workflow runs.
Retrieves structured image result fields such as title, source, thumbnail, and link.
Uses the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable for authenticated API calls.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key before use.
Depends on BrowserAct service availability and Google Images result behavior.
The script has a timeout for long-running workflow tasks.
Returned image metadata may require rights review before commercial use.

use_cases.title: Collect competitor image results
use_cases.description: Gather visual search metadata for competitor brands or product names across Google Images.

use_cases.title: Compare localized visual trends
use_cases.description: Run the same keyword in different countries and languages to compare regional image results.

use_cases.title: Build image metadata lists
use_cases.description: Create structured lists of titles, thumbnails, sources, and links for research datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Search a basic keyword
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple image metadata search.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search Google Images for "modern office chairs" in the United States and return up to 25 results.

prompt_templates.title: Run a localized search
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare image results in a specific country and language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Google Images for "electric bicycles" in Germany using German language settings, then summarize the main sources and themes.

prompt_templates.title: Gather competitor visuals
prompt_templates.scenario: Research product presentation and visual assets for a brand category.
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect Google Images metadata for three competing skincare brands, with 50 results per brand, and group the findings by source site.

prompt_templates.title: Create a regional trend comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use across multiple locales and a controlled result limit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run searches for "smart home security camera" in the United States, Japan, and France. Use local language settings where appropriate and compare thumbnail themes, product sources, and repeated domains.

output_examples.input: Search for product images for "wireless earbuds" in the United States.
output: A list of image result titles and source names.
Thumbnail URLs for each returned result.
Click-through links for product-style entries when available.

output_examples.input: Compare "coffee packaging" image results in France and Japan.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of common visual styles, recurring source domains, and notable regional differences.

output_examples.input: Find thumbnails and sources for "solar garden lights" with a limit of 30 results.
output_examples.output: Structured metadata containing result indexes, titles, source labels, thumbnails, and associated links.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY as an environment variable instead of pasting secrets into chat.
Use specific keywords and a clear country setting to reduce noisy image results.
Review image rights and source terms before reusing any returned asset.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste API keys into prompts or shared transcripts.
Do not treat returned thumbnails or links as licensed content without review.
Do not run broad searches without result limits or a clear research purpose.

faq.question: Does this skill download image files?
faq.answer: No. It returns metadata such as thumbnails, titles, source names, and links from the BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The script requires a BrowserAct API key, preferably stored in the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable.

faq.question: Can it search by country and language?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts country and language parameters supported by the skill documentation.

faq.question: Does it avoid browser automation challenges?
faq.answer: It delegates the work to a BrowserAct API workflow, so users do not manage the browser session directly.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude Code, Claude, and Codex as supported tools.

faq.question: Are the returned images safe to reuse commercially?
faq.answer: Not by default. The metadata helps discovery, but users must verify rights and source terms before reuse.
